findings.text: the log the reviewed manifest names as its declared negative control holds only the three header lines and no test output and no EXIT line, while the manifest quotes '3 failed, 2 passed in 15.34s' EXIT=1 and `reckon crew check --manifest` on that run reports it records no exit status; the mutation's red result survives only in stream.jsonl, so the artifact named for the claim cannot show it and the record refuses on its own evidence.

the recorded command is 'pytest -n 4 <13 landing-measure importer files>', an angle-bracket placeholder rather than the literal command that ran, so the base population arm cannot be re-executed from its own log and a later reader cannot check the 3 failed / 134 passed figure.

the head population log opens straight into 'bringing up nodes...' with no # command line, so the arm does not state what produced its '3 failed, 139 passed' and the delta against the base arm rests on the manifest's prose rather than on the log.

the fragment attributes '56 passed' to head cadd0db0, while gate/after-arm.log records that run at revision 33331794a6; a figure cited at a revision that did not produce it is the shape of a record that cannot be reconciled with its log.

justifications.evidence: gate/baseline-arm.log ends '51 passed ... EXIT=0' and gate/after-arm.log ends '56 passed ... EXIT=0', but gate/negative-control.log carries only its three header lines and no result.

justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:770 reads the receipt with _EXIT_RECEIPT over the whole log, so an arm whose scheduler line follows EXIT=1 yields status 1 instead of 3.
justifications.reuse: landing_measure.py:88 adds a third line-anchored EXIT= pattern beside the one owned by reckon/crew/review.py:2274 and reckon/crew/reports.py:1399 rather than extending a shared reader.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three files in the diff (landing_measure.py, the new test, the evidence fragment) are exactly the three write paths the dispatch declares.
